_comment: Context-aware prompt templates. Selected based on project type, architecture, and task.

base.header: You are working on {project_name}, a {language} project using {architecture} architecture.
base.rules_prefix: Architecture rules (flag if you need to break one):

rules: Domain layer has ZERO external dependencies — no imports from infrastructure or presentation
All external access goes through ports (interfaces) defined in domain
Infrastructure implements domain ports — never the reverse
Use cases live in application layer, not in controllers
warnings: If you need a new external service, create a port interface first
Never put business logic in controllers or infrastructure

rules: Domain is the center — adapters depend on domain, never the reverse
All I/O goes through adapter implementations of port interfaces
Ports define WHAT the domain needs, adapters define HOW
warnings: New external dependency = new adapter, never modify domain

rules: Models contain business logic and data — no view or controller dependencies
Controllers coordinate models and views — thin controllers preferred
Views only render — no business logic in templates
warnings: Fat controllers are a code smell — extract to services or models

rules: Aggregates are the consistency boundary — modify through aggregate root only
Value objects are immutable — create new instances, never mutate
Domain events capture what happened — name them in past tense
Bounded contexts are independent — communicate through events or anti-corruption layers
warnings: If an entity spans two bounded contexts, it belongs to neither — create a shared kernel or use events
Never let infrastructure concepts leak into domain (no ORM annotations in entities)

rules: Events are immutable facts — never modify a published event
Handlers must be idempotent — the same event processed twice produces the same result
Events are named in past tense (OrderPlaced, not PlaceOrder)
warnings: Avoid event chains longer than 3 steps — they become hard to debug

rules: Commands change state — queries read state — never mix
Command handlers return void or result — never return data
Read models are optimized for queries — denormalization is expected
warnings: If a query needs to trigger a side effect, it should be a command instead

rules: Each service owns its data — no shared databases
Communication between services is async when possible
API contracts are versioned — never break backward compatibility
warnings: If two services always deploy together, they should be one service

rules: Tokens are the single source of truth — never hardcode colors, spacing, or typography
Components must be accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA minimum)
Every component needs a story — if it doesn't have one, it doesn't exist
warnings: Primitives are unstyled — style through composition and tokens
Breaking changes in tokens affect ALL consumers

rules: cmd/ contains entry points only — no business logic
internal/ packages are NOT importable from outside this module
pkg/ contains reusable packages that other projects can import
warnings: Keep interfaces small — Go prefers single-method interfaces

rules: Follow convention over configuration — Rails has a place for everything
Models handle validation and business logic — keep controllers thin
Use concerns for shared behavior across models
warnings: Avoid callbacks for complex workflows — use service objects instead

rules: Each stage is independent — input from previous, output to next
Stages must not import from each other directly
New capability = new stage, not bigger existing stage
warnings: If a stage needs data from a non-adjacent stage, your pipeline design needs review

rules: Atoms are the smallest unit — they cannot import molecules or organisms
Molecules combine atoms — they cannot import organisms
Organisms are complex components — they can use molecules and atoms
Templates define page structure — they use organisms
warnings: If an atom needs props from its parent organism, the boundary is wrong

hints: Check package.json scripts before creating new build commands
Use the existing package manager ({package_manager}) — don't switch mid-project
Run bundle exec before Ruby commands
Check Gemfile for existing gems before adding new dependencies
Use cargo clippy for lint, cargo test for tests
Check Cargo.toml features before adding new dependencies
Use the existing test runner (pytest, unittest) — don't introduce another
Run go vet and go test ./... before committing
Keep error handling explicit — no panics in library code
Pattern match over conditionals when possible

rules: Changes in shared packages affect ALL workspaces — test broadly
Each workspace should be independently deployable
Keep shared dependencies in the root — workspace-specific in the workspace
warnings: Before adding a dependency to a workspace, check if it exists in root or another workspace

by_smell.god-class: This project has files >500 lines. When modifying them, consider splitting into smaller modules.
by_smell.hardcoded-secret: Secrets were detected in code. ALWAYS use environment variables for credentials.
by_smell.no-lockfile: No lockfile found. Run the package manager's lock command before committing.
